look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Plains fleabane is typically a SHORT perennial (8–40 cm) with a WOODY or LIGNIFIED taproot/crown, often persistent old stem bases. Early spring shoots can appear annual and bear a single relatively large showy head; later flowering stems often branch into many smaller heads. Lower stem hairs and ray lengths overlap E. geiseri, so a daisy-only photo is not a reliable split. Examine the mature base, seasonal branching, leaves, stem hairs and fresh phyllaries together. An uncertain plant stays Erigeron sp.

morphology_keys.root: Woody perennial taproot and persistent basal stems
morphology_keys.head: About 24-65, occasionally 170, rays 4-7 mm (sometimes 11 mm); involucre 3-4.5 mm
morphology_keys.habit: Early growth may have one large head; late growth often many smaller heads

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. geiseri has a slender annual root and characteristic lower versus upper stem hairs; rays and flowering time overlap.
comparisons.cautions: Variable polyploid complex; voucher sometimes needed. E. plateauensis and E. lobatus var. warnockii are synonyms.

field_recognition.field_split: Small annual with slender nonwoody root; lower/upper hairs overlap. Photograph roots to decide.
Early small white heads, sometimes reddish lower stems; must check woody crown, leaf bases and mature pappus.
Clasping leaf ears and many fine rays; a woody persistent crown is much more typical of mature plains fleabane.

comparisons.caution: FNA calls E. modestus a variable polyploid complex; an unclear or incomplete root/crown may require a collected voucher; no county-range certification inferred.
comparisons.root_crown_confirmation_note: The genus key contrasts mature lignified persistent crown with geiseri's slender annual root. Current E. modestus photographs show bloom and pappus, not the root crown. No licensed close-up found at the required species-specific standard; do not claim photographic closeout.

crew_field_sequence: Examine the rooted base: older woody crown and persistent basal stems are stronger clues than head color.
Inspect leaf shape and diminishing upper leaves; do not assign overlapping grass leaves in a photo to the fleabane.
Compare fresh rays, phyllaries, and fine hairs with E. geiseri using a lens and ruler.
A showy daisy-like head by itself cannot separate E. modestus from E. geiseri.
If roots are unavailable, record Erigeron sp. or a provisional comparison; preserve unresolved county native-range status.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Plains fleabane — crown before confidence
steps: The existing photo pair shows FRESH white-rayed heads versus later fluffy pappus; these are different reproductive stages.
Inspect an exposed root crown for woody older tissue, persistent stem stubs or multiple seasonal shoots.
Confirm season, branching and stem-hair pattern with a lens and ruler, comparing Geiser's annual slender root when available.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Woody persistent crown + appropriate seasonal habit supports plains fleabane. Flower rays, color or pappus alone are not decisive.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Neither installed photograph shows the diagnostic WOODY perennial crown. No false root arrow is placed.
